### A.4 The checker's known blind spots, row by row

I listed the 86 open checker rows (`python3 explorations/coordinator/tools/ledger.py heads`, filtered to open rows of area checker or specification) and read each where the checker accepts what the text or the designers refuse.

**Row 816, the reading of `abstract` (CONTESTED).** I measured it again on the landed tree with the planner's `compile-ladder/plan-22/probes/export-check-alt4i.patch` as a shadow class:

    #total 1   #kind export 1   #crash none
    (TraitDecl ReadableArray at FortressLibrary.fsi:1427.1, due to missing members ...),
    (TraitDecl ActualReduction at ...:1896.1 ...), (TraitDecl Range at ...:2189.1 ...),
    (TraitDecl String at ...:2447.1 ...), (TraitDecl AnyMaybe at ...:981.1 ...)

This is the planner's figure: 5 entries over 12 members (`CLIMB-BATCH-22.md`, question 1). So the zero rests on question 1's default, as the batch 22 review's finding 1 says. Today it costs nothing, since no compiled client reads the library. After the switch-over, a compiled call of any of the 12 through the trait's type dies with `NoSuchMethodError`, except the 3 that resolve through a parent at the same descriptor (`perf-probes/export-abstract-codegen/REPORT.md`, "In short").

**Row 782, top-level symbolic operators (NEGATIVE-BOUNDED): measured and sorted.**
- The stock check reads only `isDeclaredName` (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/scala_src/typechecker/ExportChecker.scala:275`).
- `perf-probes/export-check-full/` admits no operators, so I wrote two shadows of `ExportChecker.scala`:
  - (a) under an environment switch, `isCheckedName` in place of `isDeclaredName` at `:275`, with one line printed for each api declaration that finds no match;
  - (b) the same, plus, for every top-level operator of the api, a comparison with every component declaration of the same name, whatever key holds it, through the check's own `equalFnHeaders`.
- Results on the twelve:
  - (a): `#total 3` (`#kind export 3`, units `FortressLibrary`, `List`, `RangeInternals`, `#crash none`), with 157 "absent" entries and 9 headers that differ.
  - (b): FortressLibrary.fsi 138 match and 8 differ, List.fsi 4 and 1, RangeInternals.fsi 6 and 0. Each operator is listed twice, once under its name and once under its span key, so the raw counts are doubled.
- **The defect of the check.** The api's function relation files each top-level operator declaration under two keys: its operator name, and a name made from its span, such as `_|Library|FortressLibrary.fsi:1800:1-1801:59`. The span key can never occur in the component. The 157 "missing" entries are exactly those span keys. This is the cause that row 782's "Not traced" leaves open. It is not `equalFnHeaders`: under (b), `RangeInternals`' `SCMP` and `PCMP` match.
- **The 9 real differences:**

  | api | component | what differs |
  |---|---|---|
  | `Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:2309-2311` `opr #` ×3 → `CompactFullRange[\ZZ32\]`, `[\(ZZ32,ZZ32)\]`, `[\(ZZ32,ZZ32,ZZ32)\]` | `Library/FortressLibrary.fss:4164-4170` → `CompactFullParScalarRange`, `CompactFullRange2D`, `CompactFullRange3D` | return type |

  | `fsi:2130` `opr BIG ||(g: Generator[\Any\]): String` | `fss:3689` `opr BIG ||[\T\](g: Generator[\T\]): String` | static parameters, parameter |
  | `fsi:2137` `opr BIG |||`, likewise | `fss:3699` | the same |
  | `Library/List.fsi:114` `BIG <|[\T\]|>: Comprehension[\T,List[\T\],List[\T\],List[\T\]\]` | `Library/List.fss:178` `...,AnyCovColl,AnyCovColl\]` | return type |

- **The cost, shown on a two-file program under the compiler's prelude.** The api declares `opr #(a: String, b: String): A`. The component declares the same operator answering `B`, where `object B extends A`. A client calls `"x" # "y"`:

      bin/fortress compile P782.fss  -> rc=0     bin/fortress link P782.fss -> rc=0
      bin/fortress run P782
      REACHED pick
      Caused by: java.lang.NoSuchMethodError: 'P782Api$A P782Api.#(fortress.CompilerBuiltin$String, fortress.CompilerBuiltin$String)'

  With the component's `#` answering `A`, the same run prints `PASS`.
- **So after the switch-over**, every compiled `lo#n` and `lo:hi` reached through the api's header dies the same way, by this mechanism. `#` and `:` build every range loop. I did not run this on the one library, since no compiled program can link it yet.

The component's six `#` and `:` take the api's types, the library's own rule where the api cannot name the component's type (the `fortress-repo` skill's `library.md`, "Designing a change"). deviation: an operator is matched at its api declaration's own header, as every named function already was, where the text accepts a component declaration whose return type is a subtype (`Specification/basic/components/source-code.tex:355-360`; the check's `existsMatching`, `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/scala_src/typechecker/ExportChecker.scala:431-437`; NEW-O-1)
deviation: the speed pass restates `coverOverloading`'s cover test in the export check, since the brief leaves `OverloadingChecker.scala` untouched (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/scala_src/typechecker/ExportChecker.scala:608-621` against `OverloadingChecker.scala:843-867`)
deviation: the index's second key stays for its other readers, and the check reads past it (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/scala_src/typechecker/IndexBuilder.scala:444-446`)
historical: `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/scala_src/typechecker/ExportChecker.scala` (first edit `:275`), `Library/FortressLibrary.fsi` (`:2128`), `Library/FortressLibrary.fss` (`:4164`), `Library/List.fsi` (`:14`)

The branch is `wip/rung-export-operators`: the change with its two tests at `5046b1619`, the speed pass at `95f31de40`. The text of the change is the planner's `rung-O.patch` byte for byte (section 9, decision 1); the speed pass is mine. The harness refused the worker's write of this file and of `record.md`; their text is the run's journal.

## 1. What changed and why

**The export check.** Its loop over an api's functions admitted a name only by `isDeclaredName` (`ExportChecker.scala:274-275` at `c3c22817c`, the team's, 2012). That function takes an operator only when its name is a word of capitals, so no symbolic operator's header was ever compared (row 782). Admitting every operator is not enough on its own. `IndexBuilder.buildFunction` files each function twice: under its name, and under an unambiguous name made from its span (`IndexBuilder.scala:444-446`, the team's). An operator's span key is an `Op` that `isCheckedName` admits, and no component holds it, so every operator would be listed missing (the zero audit's shadow (a): 157 such entries). The loop now reads

    if overloadingChecker.isCheckedName(f) && isDeclarationName(fnsInAPI, f) ) {

(`ExportChecker.scala:275`). It admits every operator and every name that `isDeclaredName` admits, but only a key under which a declared function is filed by its own name (`isDeclarationName`, `:597-606`). For identifiers it admits exactly what `isDeclaredName` admitted, for two reasons. An identifier's span key, `_|...`, is no valid identifier. A key that holds no declared function gave nothing to compare before either: `coverOverloading` keeps only declared functions (`OverloadingChecker.scala:848-852`), and the other branch lists only declared functions (`ExportChecker.scala:315-323`).

**The library's 9 headers**, each stated once on both sides by the library's rule (the `fortress-repo` skill's `library.md`, "Designing a change"):
- **`#` ×3 and `:` ×3.** The component's operators answer the api's `CompactFullRange[\ZZ32\]`, `CompactFullRange[\(ZZ32,ZZ32)\]` and `CompactFullRange[\(ZZ32,ZZ32,ZZ32)\]` (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:4164-4178`). They answered `RangeInternals`' `CompactFullParScalarRange`, `CompactFullRange2D` and `CompactFullRange3D`, which the api cannot name, because `RangeInternals` imports the core api. The bodies are unchanged: `CompactFullParScalarRange` extends `CompactFullScalarRange`, and `CompactFullRange2D` extends `CompactFullRange[\(ZZ32, ZZ32)\]` (`Library/RangeInternals.fsi:494-495`, `:520-521`).
- **`BIG ||` and `BIG |||` over a generator.** The api takes the component's generic header, `[\T\](g: Generator[\T\]): String` (`Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:2128`, `:2135`). The component's declarations (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:3689`, `:3699`) have been generic since the team's tree (`a874948ac:Library/FortressLibrary.fss:3323`, `:3333`), and the team's api already states `BIG //` this way (`fsi:2142`).
- **`List`'s comprehension.** `List`'s api imports `CovariantCollection.{AnyCovColl}` and states its component's comprehension type, `Comprehension[\T,List[\T\],AnyCovColl,AnyCovColl\]` (`Library/List.fsi:14`, `:116`; the component's `Library/List.fss:178`). It named `List[\T\]` twice, the team's own mismatch since `a874948ac` (`List.fsi:110` against `List.fss:177` there).

**The speed pass** (section 5.2). With the operators read, the loop spent about 7.6 s of the count stage in `coverOverloading`. Before the change, the check never compared it.
- **`ExportOperatorMatch`**, a guard of the double key. The api declares `opr #(a: String, b: String): String`. The component declares the same, `= a || b`, and its `run()` asserts that `"x" # "y"` is `"xy"`. The `.test` file: `link`, `run`, `run_out_contains=PASS`.

## 3. Where the fix belongs, and the precedent search

The export check is the static checker's third stage and runs on a component only (`compiler/StaticChecker.java`, `checkCompilationUnit`; the skill's `compiler.md`, "The checker's time"). Its loop over the api's functions is the one place that reads an api function's header against the component's (`ExportChecker.scala:272-325`). The skip lives there, at `:275`, the file's only reader of `isDeclaredName`.

The precedent that repaired the same skip is the overloading check's (F-281). Its three loops read `isCheckedName` (`OverloadingChecker.scala:270`, `:396`, `:405`), 3 sites in its file; the export check's loop is the one site in `ExportChecker.scala`. The overloading check reads past the double key without a filter of its own: its loops read the component's own relation, where a span key holds one declaration and so overloads nothing. The export check looks a key up in the other unit's relation, where a span key can never be.

The ways for the double key:
- **(a), taken.** The check reads a key only when a declared function is filed under it by its own name (`isDeclarationName`, the planner's `opr782`).
- **(b), not taken.** `IndexBuilder.buildFunction` stops filing the second key; its team comment asks "TODO: Don't double-add the indices?" (`IndexBuilder.scala:446`). Every other reader of the relation sees that key, and the brief's fork 5 keeps it.

- **(d), not taken.** The check skips a key that is some declaration's `getUnambiguousName`. On the index as built this is equivalent to (a), but (a) states the positive condition that the loop needs.

**F-287, rewritten:**

  - Gated by `compiler_tests/XXXExportOperatorHeader`, `ExportOperatorMatch` and the distance stage's per-site list.
  - Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-export-operators/REPORT.md` sections 1, 2 and 5.3.

**F-282:** its clause "it skips every top-level operator (F-287)" becomes "it reads every top-level operator under its declared name (F-287)".

**F-281:** its clause "the export check still reads `isDeclaredName`, so it skips every top-level operator and hides 9 differences between the api and its component (row 782; F-287)" becomes "the export check reads every operator too, each under its declared name only (F-287)".

Climb batch 22c, rung O (the export check reads top-level operators), is on `wip/rung-export-operators`:
- the check admits every operator under its declared name (`5046b1619`), and its speed pass (`95f31de40`) halves the operators' cost;

## Revival change

**The change.**
- **The team's check.** The team's export check compared an api's top-level function with its component's only when the function's name was an identifier or an operator named by a word of capitals (`isDeclaredName`, `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/scala_src/typechecker/ExportChecker.scala:275` at `a874948ac`). A symbolic operator such as `#`, `:`, `+` or `BIG ||` was never compared, so a component could declare one at another header than its api's.
- **What the tree does now.** The tree compares every top-level operator by the rule it applies to any function: one component declaration at the api declaration's header, its return type included.
  - A component's `opr #(a: String, b: String): B`, with `B` extending `A`, against its api's `#` answering `A`, is refused: 'does not define all declarations' (`ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/XXXExportOperatorHeader`).
  - An operator at its api's header links and runs (`ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/ExportOperatorMatch`).
- **Against the specification.** The specification lets a component's declaration answer a subtype of the exported return type (`Specification/basic/components/source-code.tex:355-360`). So for operators, as for named functions before, the check is stricter than the text.
- **The library.** The library states one header on both sides:
  - the component's `#` and `:` answer the api's `CompactFullRange` types (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:4164-4178`);
  - the api's `BIG ||` and `BIG |||` over a generator are generic, as the team's component and the api's `BIG //` are (`Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:2128`, `:2135`, `:2142`);

- **The reason.** A compiled call names the api's header, so a component that answers a narrower type dies at the call. A two-file program whose component's `#` answers `B`, where its api's answers `A`, compiles and links, and its client's run ends `java.lang.NoSuchMethodError: 'P782Api$A P782Api.#(fortress.CompilerBuiltin$String, fortress.CompilerBuiltin$String)'`. Answering `A`, it prints `PASS`. The skipped operators hid 9 such differences in the library's twelve apis.

**Provenance.**
- P-155, "The compiled checker checks symbolic operators before the switch-over", read to cover the export check: climb batch 22c's question 2, answered option 1 by the curator ("Of course, it's option one.").
- The check's rule against the text's: question 4, built at its default (the check's rule), with NEW-O-1 `CONTESTED`.
- The double key fixed in the check rather than the index: fork 5's default. The headers by the library's rule: fork 6's default.

The export check asks its cover test only of the declared functions that its answer keeps

Climb batch 22c, rung O, its speed pass (P-148). This commit edits the
original tree: ExportChecker.scala.

With the operators read, the export check's loop over an api's functions
took about 7.6 s of the count stage, nearly all of it in
OverloadingChecker.coverOverloading on operators such as juxtaposition,
-, = and CMP, whose sets hold many functional methods that the answer
then drops. uncoveredDeclarations gives the same answer and asks the
cover test only of the declared functions: an audit on the count stage
found its answer equal to coverOverloading's at all 144 names, and the
loop took about 3.8 s. The count stage's table and output are those of
the change.

content.content:
Export statements specify the APIs that a component exports.
One important restriction on components is that no \apiN\ may be both
imported and exported by the same component. This restriction helps to
avoid some (but not all) accidental cyclic dependencies.

Every component implicitly imports the Fortress core APIs;
every fortress has at least one component implementing all of these \apisN.
A \emph{preferred} component exporting these \apisN\ (configurable by the user)
is implicitly linked to
every component installed in the fortress.


A component must provide a declaration, or a set of declarations,
that \emph{satisfies} every top-level declaration in any API
that it exports, as described below.
A component may include declarations
that do not participate in satisfying any exported declaration
(i.e., a declaration of any exported API), and in particular,
no declaration modified by \KWD{private}
participates in satisfying any exported declaration.
Such declarations are not visible from outside the component.

Type aliases and dimension, unit, test and property declarations
are satisfied only by declarations that are the same.\footnote{The
declarations are compared after ASCII conversion and scanning,
and differences in the characters within whitespace elements
is permitted
provided they do not change whether the whitespace element
is line-breaking.
}
\note{Victor: what about trait/object/etc declarations with test modifier?}

A top-level variable declaration declaring a single variable
is satisfied by any top-level variable declaration
that declares the name with the same type
(in the component,
the type may be inferred).
A top-level variable declaration declaring multiple variables
is satisfied by a set of declarations (possibly just one)
that declare all the names with their respective types
(which again, may be inferred).
In either case,
the modifiers including the mutability of a variable must be the same in
the exported and satisfying declarations.
A top-level variable declaration
declaring a single immutable variable
with arrow type \EXP{P \rightarrow R}
is also satisfied
by a set of top-level function and functional method declarations
if the union of their parameter types is \VAR{P}
and each of their return types is a subtype of \VAR{R}.
Thus, an abstract function declaration
in the form of variable declarations in an API
need not be replicated in a component exporting that API.

A top-level function declaration is satisfied by
a set of top-level function and functional method declarations
the union of whose parameter types
is the parameter type of the exported declaration,
and each of whose return types
is a subtype of the return type of the exported declaration.
\note{Victor: also need type of thrown checked exceptions

Victor: it may also be satisfied by a declaration
 or set of declarations whose parameter type is a supertype
 of the exported declaration's parameter type
 provided that there is an overloaded exported declaration
 whose parameter type is a supertype of the satisfying declarations.
 (This comment also applied to the method declarations below.
 We need a term for this concept.)
}

A trait or object declaration is satisfied by
a declaration
that has the same header,\footnote{The order of
the modifiers,
the clauses,
and the types in the
\KWD{extends}, \KWD{excludes} and \KWD{comprises} clauses
may differ.}
and contains,
for each field declaration and non-abstract method declaration
in the exported declaration,
a satisfying declaration (or a set of declarations).
When a trait has an abstract method declared,
a satisfying trait declaration is allowed to provide a concrete declaration.
If a trait declaration (in an API)
has a \KWD{comprises} clause containing ``\EXP{\ldots}'',
then the \KWD{comprises} clause of its satisfying declaration
must contain all the types listed in the declaration in the API
but it cannot contain ``\EXP{\ldots}'';
instead, it may contain other types declared in the component
provided that those types are not declared by the API.
A field declaration is satisfied by
a (possibly implicit) getter and/or setter declaration,
depending on whether the field
is declared to be \KWD{hidden} and/or \KWD{settable}
by the exported declaration.

A method declaration is satisfied
by a set of method declarations
the union of whose parameter types
is the parameter type of the exported declaration,
and each of whose return types
is a subtype of the return type of the exported declaration.
\note{
Victor: need to be dotted iff exported decl is dotted.

Victor: also need type of thrown checked exceptions}
A satisfying trait or object declaration
may contain method and field declarations not exported by the API

If a trait declaration of \VAR{T} includes a \KWD{comprises} clause

\subsection{Traits with comprises clauses read at the level of values}
\seclabel{revival-covering}

\begin{description}
\item[Affected sections] \secref{internal-types};
\secref{abstractFunctionDeclarations}; \secref{methods}; a draft note in the
subsection ``Export Statements'' of \secref{components}; the effect of
\secref{revival-comprises}.
\item[Change] \secref{internal-types} defines covering: a type covers another
when every value of the second is a value of the first; a type covers each of
its subtypes, and a trait with a \KWD{comprises} clause is covered by the union
of its listed types; covering is not the subtype relation.
Its example concludes that $V$ covers $S \inter T$, where it concluded that
$V = S \inter T$, and a sentence says that a trait may stand between $S$ or $T$
and their listed types, so that $S \inter T$ is not in general equal to a named
type.
\secref{abstractFunctionDeclarations} asks the argument types of the concrete
declarations to cover the argument type of the abstract declaration, where it
asked their union to equal it, and, in its example, for a definition for every
type listed in the \KWD{comprises} clause of \TYP{Molecule} or definitions that
together cover those types, where it asked for one for every immediate subtype.
Each of these four passages has a box.
The draft note says ``all its listed types'' where it said ``all its immediate
subtraits''; a draft note prints only in a draft build, so it has no box.
The effect of \secref{revival-comprises} no longer says that these passages are
not revised.
A correction of 9~October 2026 changes the last sentence of the box after the
example in \secref{abstractFunctionDeclarations} and the sentence of this

== explorations/fortress-gap-ledger.md:7-27

## The row template

A row is one line of eight cells, `| # | claim | status | class | spec citation | reproducer | found by | notes / workaround |`, at most 1,200 characters, in the table of its topic section, in number order. A pipe inside a cell is written `\|`. (POSITIONS, "The gap ledger's form"; the proposal behind it is `explorations/coordinator/process-engineering/gap-ledger-archaeology.md`, section 4.)

- **#**: the row's number, the next free one when it is added; never reused, renumbered or given to another row. 148 is vacant.
- **claim**: at most 300 characters, whose first 150 name the defect or the capability: what fails or what holds, and where.
- **status**: exactly one word of seven, with no second status and nothing in brackets:
  - `POSITIVE-VERIFIED`: it works; it ran and its output is recorded.
  - `NEGATIVE-VERIFIED`: the specification settles it and the reproducer confirms it. A row with one half fixed stays `NEGATIVE-VERIFIED`, and its notes say which half is fixed.
  - `NEGATIVE-BOUNDED`: the failure reproduces; the mechanisms tried are named and are not exhaustive.
  - `CONTESTED`: unsettled; the notes say why.
  - `RETIRED`: a source's claim falsified here, kept so that it is not derived again.
  - `FIXED`: closed by a landed commit (`ledger.py close`): the claim's first sentence, the test as reproducer, notes `fixed HASH; full text: history, row N`.
  - `DUPLICATE`: a pointer (`ledger.py duplicate`), notes `duplicate of row M; full text: history, row N`.
- **class**: `kind (area)`; `—` only for `POSITIVE-VERIFIED` and `RETIRED`. The kind is one of `implementation gap`, `library gap vs spec`, `library bug`, `design limit`, `deliberate`, `typesetter`, `packaging`; the area one of `parser`, `walk`, `checker`, `codegen`, `runtime`, `library`, `prelude`, `specification`, `tests`, `tools`.
- **spec citation**: the `.tex` file and the section heading in quotes, as `basic/operators/juxtameaning.tex`, "Juxtaposition"; a line number only against `Specification-1.0-frozen/`; `silent` where the specification does not say.
- **reproducer**: one test (its name, or its path under the test folders; an `XXX` test while it is an expected failure) or one probe path from the repository root, at most 200 characters; `none` when nothing in the tree reproduces it, with the command and its output, or the probe's old path, in the notes.
- **found by**: the stream that found it (`climb batch 8 rung I`, `run-c3`, `apl rung 2`), at most 60 characters; no date and no role.
- **notes / workaround**: at most 700 characters: `siblings: N, M` first if there are any; the mechanism, with file:line and the commit it was true at; the workaround; for a closed row, `fixed HASH`.

A path under `explorations/` that is no longer in the tree is read from history: `git show $(git log -1 --diff-filter=D --format=%h -- PATH)^:PATH`.
